sections.html:
Lawrence is a city on the northeast side of Indianapolis, in Lawrence Township, Marion County. Downtown Indianapolis is about 9 miles to the southwest, and Hancock County, including the town of McCordsville, borders the city on the east.

The city covers about 20.2 square miles. Fall Creek, a tributary of the White River, runs through the northwest part and forms part of the boundary, and Fort Harrison State Park fills much of that corner.

The Census Bureau puts the 2025 population at 50,420, up from 49,370 in the 2020 count. In 2020 there were 19,067 households and the median age was 35.9.

sections.h2: How is Lawrence governed if it is part of Indianapolis?
sections.html:
Lawrence is one of four excluded cities under Unigov, the 1969 merger of Indianapolis and Marion County, which means it kept its own municipal government. The mayor is Deborah Whitfield, and the Common Council has six district seats and three at-large seats.

Residents of Lawrence still vote for the Indianapolis mayor and the Indianapolis City-County Council. For a seller, the practical point is that city rules on code compliance and permits come from Lawrence, while county services such as the property tax bill and recording come from Marion County.

Lawrence grew from 38,915 residents in 2000 to 46,001 in 2010 and 49,370 in 2020. That steady rise created a mix of housing ages, from older homes near the original town center to newer subdivisions farther out.

The city uses ZIP codes 46216, 46226, 46235 and 46236, and the area codes are 317 and 463. The elevation is about 853 feet.

The school district reported a 92.7 percent high school graduation rate for 2018 to 2019, according to the district's reference entry.

The settlement was platted in 1849 as Lanesville, a name another Indiana town already held, so it became Jamestown, after founder James White. In 1866 the Marion County Commissioners approved the name Lawrence, for Captain James Lawrence, a naval hero of the War of 1812.

Residents voted to become an independent town in 1929 and set up a town marshal and other offices.

The biggest local chapter is the fort. Fort Benjamin Harrison operated as a U.S. Army post from 1906 until 1991, and the 1991 Base Realignment and Closure Commission ended its role. The site has since been redeveloped with residential neighborhoods, a golf course and Fort Harrison State Park.

sections.h2: What does Fort Harrison mean for the area today?
sections.html:
The former post still shapes the northeast edge of Lawrence. The Fort Benjamin Harrison Historic District, listed on the National Register in 1995, covers about 360 acres and includes 100 contributing buildings, many in Colonial Revival brick.

  • The Defense Finance and Accounting Service in Indianapolis, Army Reserve and Marine Corps Reserve detachments, and Indiana National Guard units remain at the former post.
  • The Lawrence Readiness Training Center opened in 2011.
  • The American Legion's operations center has been there since 1999, and the VFW Department of Indiana has its headquarters on East 59th Street.

Fort Harrison State Park covers 1,700 acres, with trails, a nature center, fishing access to Fall Creek and a golf course. If your house sits near the historic district, ask the city whether any local review applies before you plan exterior work.

sections.h2: What are the roads and commutes like?
sections.html:
U.S. 36, Pendleton Pike, runs through Lawrence and continues about 22 miles northeast to Pendleton. Interstate 465, the Indianapolis beltway, meets U.S. 36 at Exit 42 in the southwest corner, and Exit 40 at East 56th Street and North Shadeland Avenue lies along the western border.

The beltway puts the rest of the Indianapolis metro within a drive, which is the main reason Lawrence is treated as part of that market.

The Metropolitan School District of Lawrence Township runs public K-12 education. It was established in 1959 and enrolls about 16,165 students.

  • Two high schools: Lawrence Central and Lawrence North.
  • Two middle schools and eleven elementary schools.
  • Four kindergarten centers and one alternative school.
  • Eight National Blue Ribbon Schools.

The district office is at 6501 Sunnyside Rd. Ivy Tech Community College also has a campus in Lawrence.

sections.h2: What is the climate, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Lawrence has a humid continental climate with hot, humid summers and mild to cold winters. Annual precipitation averages about 46.6 inches, with June the wettest month at 5.96 inches and February the driest at 2.90 inches.

Wet springs and summers test basements, sump pumps, gutters and grading. If your lot is close to Fall Creek, look up the flood zone before you list, since insurers and lenders check it.

sections.h2: How does Lawrence code enforcement work?
sections.html:
The Division of Code Compliance, inside the Department of Public Works, enforces municipal code in Lawrence. According to the city's code enforcement page, it covers minimum property maintenance standards, building codes, permitting requirements and licensing, and it works toward voluntary compliance.

  • Address: 9001 East 59th Street, Lawrence, IN 46216
  • Phone: (317) 545-6191
  • Violations can be reported through a link on the city site

If you own a vacant or neglected house in Lawrence, a notice from this office is a common starting point for a sale. An as-is buyer takes over the repairs and the compliance conversation.

sections.h2: How are a sale and deed handled in Marion County?
sections.html:
Because Lawrence sits in Marion County, a deed is recorded with the Marion County Recorder after the sales disclosure form is completed. Under Indiana Code 6-1.1-5.5-3, the parties to the conveyance complete the form, the county assessor approves it, and the auditor processes any deduction.

The state sets property tax due dates in Indiana Code 6-1.1-22-9: May 10 and November 10 of the following year. Ask your closing agent how the current installment will be split between you and the buyer. Your tax bill is the place to check which installments are already paid.

sections.h2: What do Lawrence sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Many owners sell because of inherited homes, rental headaches, repair backlogs or a move. Lawrence is a city of about 50,000 people inside a much larger metro area, so a listing competes with homes across Marion County and the surrounding counties.

  • A traditional listing needs prep, showings and a buyer who clears financing and inspection.
  • A for-sale-by-owner route saves commission and adds paperwork and marketing work.
  • A cash sale lets you skip repairs and set the closing date.

Compare net proceeds across the three before choosing.

faqs.q: Is Lawrence, Indiana part of Indianapolis?
faqs.a: Lawrence is in Marion County and borders Indianapolis, but it is an excluded city under Unigov and keeps its own government. Residents still vote in Indianapolis city elections.

faqs.q: Who handles code violations in Lawrence?
faqs.a: The Division of Code Compliance in the Department of Public Works. It is at 9001 East 59th Street, and the phone is (317) 545-6191.
The Metropolitan School District of Lawrence Township, with Lawrence Central and Lawrence North high schools. Confirm the district for your exact address.

faqs.q: When are Indiana property taxes due?
faqs.a: State law sets installments on May 10 and November 10. Marion County's treasurer can confirm the exact dates and any weekend adjustment.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my Lawrence house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so repairs and cleaning stay with the buyer.

faqs.q: What is Fort Harrison State Park?
faqs.a: It is a 1,700 acre park on the former Fort Benjamin Harrison, with trails, a nature center, fishing access to Fall Creek and a golf course, run by the Indiana DNR.
